messages.content: Help me execute a callback function named 'processResult' that handles an error 'null' and a result value of 'Operation successful'?

function.name: invokeCallback
function.description: This function invokes a callback with an error and a value. If the callback throws an error, it is caught and re-thrown asynchronously. Note that the provided function is in JavaScript syntax.

callback.description: The callback function to be invoked. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

error.description: The error to pass to the callback function. Can be 'null' if there is no error. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

value.description: The value to pass to the callback function. This parameter can be of any type of JavaScript object in string representation.

message.reasoning:
We need to use the tool "invokeCallback" from functions namespace. Provide JSON input with fields: callback (string), error (string), value (string). We want to call processResult(null, 'Operation successful'). So we set callback as "function(err, val) { /* code */ }"? But they said help me execute a callback function named 'processResult', so maybe just provide invocation? According to spec, we should supply the callback function itself as string. They might expect us to write something like:

{
  "callback": "(err, res)=>{ console.log('Error:', err); console.log('Result:', res); }",
  "error":"null",
  "value":"'Operation successful'"
}

But the description says "The callback function to be invoked." It could be name or actual function body. Usually they'd give JS snippet.

Let's produce output calling the function. We'll include the function definition inside the callback field. Use arrow function. For error null, value string.
